entities.summary: Moshe Ya'akov Vardi is an Israeli theoretical computer scientist. He is the Karen Ostrum George Distinguished Service Professor in Computational Engineering at Rice University, United States. and a faculty advisor for the Ken Kennedy Institute. His interests focus on applications of logic to computer science, including database theory, finite model theory, knowledge of multi-agent systems, computer-aided verification and reasoning, and teaching logic across the curriculum. He is an expert in model checking, constraint satisfaction and database theory, common knowledge (logic), and theoretical computer science.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Moshe Vardi's work on logic and theoretical computer science has had a significant impact on database theory and finite model theory, with applications in multi-agent systems and computer-aided verification. His research has also influenced the development of knowledge representation and reasoning.
